To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integration of language and content is best understood as the combination of two main variables: the functions of the language in the different subjects (subject literacy and genres) and students' engagement with language and content in classroom interactional activities.

the successful learning of content and language in CLIL requires: (1) a good understanding of how the two variables (subject genres and classroom interaction) are integrated and how they interact; and (2) the use of an integrated pedagogical approach that considers both language and content.
CLIL learners need to be able to integrate language and content to be academically successful in a foreign language.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the linguistic features of the different subjects that are integrated in CLIL?
the study of the interactional activities that take place in the classroom and their role in content and language integration.
the question of what and how integration in CLIL is.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
integration in CLIL is the result of the combination of the knowledge of what is integrated and how this knowledge is learnt in the classroom.

CLIL learners are engaged in the integration of language and content when they are aware of how language functions to make meanings in their academic discipline, when they use the language of their discipline in the foreign language and when they interact in different activities with the purpose of learning both the language of the subject and the content of the subject in a meaningful way.
the study of integration requires an approach that considers both the linguistic and the interactional aspects of the classroom.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CLIL students need to be able to integrate the linguistic resources required by their academic disciplines and also to integrate their participation in classroom activities.

integration can be understood as the combination of two main variables: the subject literacies and genres of a particular discipline and the way these literacies and genres are learnt in the context of the classroom, through the participation in a variety of interactional activities.

CLIL learners' integration is best understood when we consider the functions of language and meaning in different academic disciplines (SFL) as well as the way these functions are realised in different classroom interactional activities (interactional approaches to learning).
The main takeaway from our work is that
CLIL students need to be aware that language and content can be learnt in integration and that the way they participate in the classroom is key to the learning of content and language.
integration in CLIL needs to be understood from two different angles: the functions of the language in the subjects and how these functions interact in the context of classroom activities.
integration is not only a question of what is being integrated but also a question of how it is being integrated.
